newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares buoyed by political optimism.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares buoyed by political optimism.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose 1.09 percent on Wednesday as investors returned to the bourse, sensing a political rapprochement after the election of a new parliamentary president went without a hitch.

Late on Tuesday, parliament voted almost unanimously for Janez Podbonik of the conservative People's Party, part of the rightist "Spring" alliance that had set its sights on ousting Liberal Democrat Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek.
"The election of Podobnik...could mean that the two blocs have reached an agreement that would allow Drnovsek to remain as prime minister" said Goran Brankovic, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska banka.
The 10-share SBI index climbed 12.72 points to 1,180.0, recovering some of the 4.2 percent loss since November's inconclusive general election.
Brankovic noted that Drnovsek, a strong supporter of European Union membership, had the best credentials to attract foreign investors.
Turnover jumped to 258.3 million tolars from 78.9 million. Overall 12 shares rose and six fell, while seven were untraded.
Drug maker Lek A issue was the most active share, rising 3.95 percent to 19,750 tolars on volume of 5,775 shares.
"Foreigners contributed a lot to today's jump in turnover, mostly by buying Lek's shares," one trader said.
Preferred shares of Hipotekarna banka Brezice were the biggest gainer, firming 4.71 percent to 4,000 tolars on volume of 20 shares.
Ordinary shares of Dolenjska bank were the leading decliner, falling 2.42 percent to 11,700 on volume of 140 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
